units.translation: The season of trees is complete from the moistening marriage.
I wet my cheek with moist streams.
moisture blowing upon the dry wheel: on which passage see under προσαυρίζω.
Διὸς νότῳ [by the south wind of Zeus] is corrupt for διοσδότῳ [given by Zeus], which see.
And this Aegina lies toward the blasts of the south wind.
by the south wind of Zeus
to advise and admonish the one who is faring badly.
You are made wise by reasonable admonitions.
There is hope that a nocturnal end will come.
I know the assembly of the nocturnal stars.
they have the forms of nocturnal apparitions
to speak or act by night
The active is used of the guards in Rhesus v. 89 φύλακες νυκτηγοροῦσι [the guards keep watch by night].

Passive Sept. 29: This man (Tiresias), master of such prophecies, says that a great Achaean assault and plot against the city is being carried on by night. Thus I corrected what is read in M νυκτηγορεῖσθαι κἀπιβουλεύσειν (κἀπιβουλεύειν in the copies) against the city, which the scholiast also read, wrongly interpreting it as 'to be spoken and planned in the night'.
the guards keep watch by night
But my anxious thought remains to hear something, hidden by night.
the toil of battle, wandering by night
I have a bed that is night-wandering and dewy.
and from dreams and night-wandering terrors I am shaken
of night-wandering shrill commands. Schol.: not only by day, but also by night.
revered in the night, holy by night
revered in the night, holy by night
night-holy feasts. In M νυκτὶ σεμνά [holy in the night], two words; corrected by Turnebus.
night-roaming dreams, where M has νυκτίφαντ᾽ [appearing by night], but the copies have νυκτίφοιτ᾽, which seems correct: on which I have spoken under δεῖμα p. 78b.
keeping watch by night, vigilant at night
keeping watch by night, vigilant at night
I gather for the Nymphs of the springs, the glorious goddesses,
Lady Nymph, queen of the stormy mountains
But for the one who touches (thus Scaliger for οἴγοντι) there is no remedy from the bridal chambers.
madness brings together bridegrooms who are frenzied in mind.
let them make the bridegrooms gracious by the laws
lamented by brides, causing bridal tears
lamented by brides, causing bridal tears
The genitive νυκτός is used adverbially: by night.
There is one example of the plural.
this night which you speak of, gleaming with stars on the shield (on the shield of Tydeus), to be in the sky
For if night would fall upon the eyes of the dead.
if the darkness of black night comes
